class.name: FmodAudioEffectCompressor
class.brief_description: Dynamic range compressor for reducing the dynamic range of audio signals.
class.description: FmodAudioEffectCompressor is a dynamic range compression effect that reduces the volume of loud sounds while leaving quiet sounds unchanged. It is commonly used to control dynamics, prevent clipping, and make audio more consistent in loudness. The compressor works by measuring the input level and reducing gain when it exceeds a specified threshold. The amount of reduction is determined by the ratio, and the response time is controlled by attack and release parameters. This effect supports makeup gain and a dry/wet mix for parallel compression. Sidechain routing is not implemented; setting [member sidechain] only stores the requested bus name.

members.member: The threshold level in decibels (dB) above which compression begins. Range: -60 dB to 0 dB. Default: 0 dB. Signals below this level pass through unaffected; signals above are reduced according to the ratio. Lower threshold values result in more compression.
The compression ratio, clamped to 1.0 through 48.0. The default is 4.0: for every 4 dB the input exceeds the threshold, the output increases by 1 dB.
The makeup gain applied after compression, in decibels. Clamped to -20.0 through +20.0 dB; the default is 0.0 dB.

The requested attack time in microseconds, clamped to 20.0 through 2000.0. The stored default is 20.0 microseconds. The value is converted to milliseconds for FMOD and clamped to a minimum of 0.1 ms, so requests below 100 microseconds use an effective attack time of 100 microseconds.
The release time in milliseconds, clamped to 20.0 through 2000.0. The default is 250.0 ms. It controls how quickly compression recovers after the input level falls below the threshold.

The mix between dry (unprocessed) and wet (compressed) signal, as a value from 0.0 to 1.0. Default: 1.0 (fully wet). A value of 0.0 outputs only the dry signal, 1.0 outputs only the compressed signal, and intermediate values blend the two. This enables parallel compression effects.
Stores a requested sidechain bus name. Sidechain routing is not implemented, so this property does not change which signal controls compression. The default is an empty name.
